name: ClickDetector
simple: A ClickDetector lets players click (or tap) on a part in the 3D world. Put one inside a part, and its MouseClick event fires when someone clicks that part, telling you who clicked. It also knows when the mouse moves over the part or right-clicks it.
analogy: A ClickDetector is like turning a part into a big real-life button. Without it, a part is just a block; with it, the part can feel your clicks.
whenToUse: Buttons in the world, like an elevator button or a light switch.
Click a chest, NPC, or item to interact with it.
Change the mouse icon or glow a part when the mouse hovers over it.
where: Put it inside a BasePart, Model, or Folder in Workspace. Its events fire in both Scripts (server) and LocalScripts (client). For a LocalScript, put the script in StarterPlayerScripts, not inside the ClickDetector.

terms.hover: When the mouse pointer is over something without clicking.
terms.cursor: The mouse pointer on the screen.
terms.asset ID: The address of an uploaded image or file, like `rbxassetid://123456`.
terms.server: Roblox's computer running the shared game.
terms.deprecated: Old and replaced by something newer.

examples.title: Light switch
examples.place: Script inside a Part named Switch (with a ClickDetector inside it, and a PointLight in a Part named Lamp)
examples.code:
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local switch = script.Parent
local detector = switch:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")
local light = Workspace:WaitForChild("Lamp"):WaitForChild("PointLight")

detector.MaxActivationDistance = 15 -- must be within 15 studs

detector.MouseClick:Connect(function(player)
	light.Enabled = not light.Enabled -- flip on/off
	print(player.Name, "flipped the switch")
end)
explain: MouseClick fires on the server with the player who clicked.
`not light.Enabled` flips true to false or false to true, so each click toggles the light.
Because this is a server Script, everyone sees the light change.

examples.title: Glow on hover
examples.place: Script inside a Part (with a ClickDetector inside it)
examples.code:
local part = script.Parent
local detector = part:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")

detector.MouseHoverEnter:Connect(function()
	part.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
end)

detector.MouseHoverLeave:Connect(function()
	part.Material = Enum.Material.Plastic
end)
explain: When the mouse moves onto the part, it turns glowing Neon.
When the mouse leaves, it turns back to Plastic.

gotchas: A LocalScript inside a ClickDetector in Workspace will not run. Put LocalScripts in StarterPlayerScripts and find the detector from there.
Players farther than MaxActivationDistance cannot click it.
If several ClickDetectors could catch a click, only the deepest one (most nested) fires.

ClickDetector.CursorIcon.simple: The image used for the mouse pointer while it hovers over the part. Leave empty for the default pointer.
ClickDetector.CursorIcon.example:
local detector = script.Parent:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")
detector.CursorIcon = "rbxassetid://0000000" -- use your own image ID

ClickDetector.CursorIconContent.simple: Same idea as CursorIcon (the hover mouse image), but stored as a Content value. It only accepts asset addresses.

ClickDetector.MaxActivationDistance.simple: How close, in studs, a player's character must be to click it. If a character is 10 studs away and this is 5, the click does not count.

ClickDetector.MouseClick.simple: Fires when a player left-clicks the part (or taps it on a phone, or presses the controller button while aiming at it). Gives you the player who clicked.

ClickDetector.MouseHoverEnter.simple: Fires when a player's mouse pointer moves onto the part. Gives you that player.
ClickDetector.MouseHoverEnter.example:
local detector = script.Parent:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")
detector.MouseHoverEnter:Connect(function(player)
	print(player.Name, "is pointing at me")
end)

ClickDetector.MouseHoverLeave.simple: Fires when a player's mouse pointer moves off the part.
ClickDetector.MouseHoverLeave.example:
local detector = script.Parent:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")
detector.MouseHoverLeave:Connect(function(player)
	print(player.Name, "stopped pointing at me")
end)

ClickDetector.RightMouseClick.simple: Fires when a player right-clicks the part. Gives you the player.
